transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-08
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Samantha Lee (Aurora CISO), Rajiv Nair (Aurora Head of Platform), Elena Gomez (Aurora Cloud Eng)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Aurora Education is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployments. Primary concerns: student data residency (US-only), FERPA compliance, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML with their Okta instance, RBAC for multi-tenant schools, audit logging retention (7 years requested), and deletion/retention workflows. They want a pilot timeline in 4-6 weeks and a cost-latency tradeoff discussion to decide between Hosted + VPC or Redwood Private.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:08] Samantha (Aurora): Hey, Samantha here, CISO for Aurora.
[00:11] Rajiv (Aurora): Rajiv, head of platform.
[00:14] Elena (Aurora): Elena, cloud eng, I run our infra and Okta integration work.
[00:18] Diego (Redwood): Diego, solutions engineer. I'll take the deeper infra questions.
[00:22] Maya: Awesome. The plan for today is to go over security posture requirements, hosting options—hosted, dedicated, private—and KMS/SSO needs. We'll capture action items and next steps.
[00:33] Samantha: Great. To start: our top-line requirement is we host all student PII within US regions only. FERPA requires certain controls, and our legal wants 7 years of audit logs retained for investigations.
[00:44] Rajiv: Also, any managed service we use needs to integrate with our Okta SAML idp and support SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. We try to avoid any vendor-managed keys for PII—prefer customer-managed KMS or HSM.
[00:56] Diego: Understood. Redwood supports hosted (multi-tenant API), dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and private (customer VPC or on-prem). For KMS we offer BYOK via cloud KMS integrations; we also have an HSM option for Private deployments.
[01:10] Elena: When you say BYOK for hosted, do you mean keys are in our cloud account or you store them?
[01:15] Diego: For Hosted, we typically provide envelope encryption where the data keys are encrypted with a Redwood-managed root key unless you opt for a customer-managed key via an external KMS provider. For strict requirements, Private deployment with KMS in your account or HSM backing in your VPC is the recommended pattern.
[01:30] Samantha: So hosted with CMK is possible? Or is that only for Dedicated/Private?
[01:35] Maya: We do offer hosted + customer-managed key where you grant Redwood a key encryption key in your cloud KMS, but because of policy constraints some customers prefer Private so the control plane doesn't have access to plaintext keys. It's a spectrum.
[01:46] Rajiv: That spectrum is exactly our problem. Legal will push back if Redwood can decrypt tokens for debugging. We need cryptographic separation and an auditable key access policy.
[01:56] Diego: That makes sense. For Private we run the inference runtime inside your VPC and keys never leave your account; Redwood's control plane only sees metadata. For Dedicated, you can also bring a CMK in a dedicated account model where keys live in your cloud tenant.
[02:12] Elena: Is there an HSM-backed KMS option for Dedicated? We've had trouble with some vendors who only offer software KMS.
[02:18] Diego: HSM-backed KMS is available for Private and in some Dedicated offerings as an add-on; depends on contract and region. I'll follow up with the sales engineering SKU details.
[02:28] Samantha: Audit logs—we need immutability and 7-year retention. Do you have WORM or append-only logs? How are they exported?
[02:36] Maya: We support exporting audit logs to your cloud logging account (e.g., Cloud Logging or Log Analytics), and we can stream to S3/GCS with lifecycle policies. For immutability, we rely on your retention controls—Redwood can push logs to a write-once bucket in your account if desired.
[02:52] Rajiv: Ok, so the canonical logs live in our cloud. Who signs the attestations for SOC2/ISO? Legal wants the latest reports.
[03:00] Maya: We can share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations; those are signed by our external auditors. I'll attach the PDFs afterward.
[03:07] Samantha: Please do. We will need the scope — specifically, does the SOC2 scope include private deployments and any managed key handling?
[03:13] Diego: Our SOC2 covers Redwood’s hosted control plane and production services. Private deployments where Redwood manages the runtime in a customer's VPC are typically scoped differently—I'll include a note in the package clarifying scope boundaries.
[03:27] Elena: On SSO, we use Okta SAML and expect SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. Also SCIM for user provisioning and group sync to map school admins vs teachers.
[03:39] Diego: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM. RBAC can be mapped from groups. We currently support role templates and custom roles—again mapping groups from SCIM is common practice.
[03:49] Rajiv: Do roles support limiting access to datasets or model endpoints per customer tenant? We host multiple K‑12 districts and need strict separation.
[03:57] Diego: Yes, RBAC can be scoped by organization and route. For hosted multi-tenant we provide strict logical isolation; for stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated/Private with network-level segmentation.
[04:09] Samantha: Data retention & deletion: We need ability to delete a student record across caches, logs, and backups within 72 hours of request, and also demonstrate deletion to auditors. How do you handle KV caches and model contexts?
[04:21] Diego: Good question. For inference state like KV caches, we support explicit deletion APIs and TTLs. For model contexts stored transiently, we avoid persistent storage by default in Hosted. For Dedicated/Private, we can provide deletion playbooks and ensure backups are purged according to policy. I'll capture a technical doc reference in the follow-up.
[04:39] Elena: Can you guarantee deletion from model fine-tuning or usage logs—like if we used logs for evals?
[04:44] Maya: We don't fine-tune customer models on pooled corpora unless agreed; logs used for quality or eval are redacted and can be disabled. We'll include the exact data flows in the security pack.
[04:55] Samantha: Incident response: we need SLA for breach notification and a runbook. What is your timeline for notifying customers?
[05:02] Maya: Standard is 72 hours for incidents with customer impact, but for PII we do prioritized notifications. We operate an incident management system and can share a summary of our IR playbook.
[05:11] Rajiv: Encryption in transit: TLS ok, but we need mTLS for internal service-to-service where possible. Does Redwood support mTLS between your control plane and customer VPC connectors?
[05:21] Diego: Yes, for Private we use mutual TLS for control-plane connectors and signed certs; for Dedicated we can set up mTLS depending on networking topology.
[05:29] Samantha: Backups—where are they stored and encrypted? Are they in our account for Private?
[05:34] Diego: For Private they can be in your account and encrypted with your CMK. For Hosted, backups are encrypted at rest and managed, but you can request export and hold copies in your tenant for compliance.
[05:45] Elena: Regarding latency sensitivity, some of our interactive features can't tolerate >200ms p95. If we go Private in-region, how do you measure and guarantee latency?
[05:55] Diego: We provide latency SLOs per model profile and region; Dedicated/Private gives better tail latency because you control network hops and GPU locality. We'll share perf profiles and real measurements from our benchmarks.
[06:06] Samantha: What's the typical contract minimum for Dedicated or Private? We need to budget and justify to procurement.
[06:12] Maya: Dedicated often has monthly reserved commits (e.g., X GPUs) with a 12-month minimum; Private has an enterprise license and support fee—I'll send typical ranges to help budget.
[06:21] Rajiv: One more: auditability of admin actions — who changed RBAC, who accessed keys, who exported data. Do you provide an immutable admin audit trail?
[06:31] Diego: Yes, admin audit trails are part of our console and can be exported. For Private, logs go to your logging account and can be retained per your retention policy.
[06:40] Samantha: Are there any certifications you do not meet that would be blockers? For example, we require SOC2 and ISO 27001 and prefer an annual penetration test report.
[06:49] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. We also run annual pen tests and can provide summaries and remediation tickets. If there's a specialized federation or country-specific compliance we can discuss.
[06:58] Elena: Ok on the SOC2. We'll need the scope and the last pen test report redacted for sensitive details.
[07:04] Maya: We'll prepare a security pack with SOC2/ISO PDFs, redacted pentest summary, RBAC docs, KMS/HSM options, and data flow diagrams.
[07:12] Samantha: For data residency: Are there any multi-region failovers where data could leave the US? Our SLA requires failover within US-only regions and documented guarantees.
[07:23] Diego: We can pin region affinity and configure failover to US regions only. For Hosted, some control plane operations could be multi-region, but we can provide contractual language about data plane locality. For Private, you control region pins.
[07:38] Rajiv: If we choose hosted with CMK, we still want zero-knowledge of customer plaintext keys. Can Redwood ever request decrypt access for debugging?
[07:46] Maya: We do have support workflows that may request ephemeral access in rare cases, but we can formalize an escrow process with strict approvals. For strict zero-knowledge, Private with keys in your account is the recommended path.
[07:58] Elena: What about developer access? We have internal devs who will need to call the API. Can we limit token scopes and rotate frequently?
[08:05] Diego: Yes, token-level RBAC, short-lived tokens, and key rotation are supported. We also offer service principals and scoped API keys with route-level permissions.
[08:14] Samantha: Any references to FERPA-specific handling? We need attestation that the service aligns with FERPA, specifically on access controls for student records.
[08:23] Maya: We don't provide a FERPA cert per se, but we can provide controls mapping and evidence showing access control, encryption, and logging which you can include in your vendor risk assessment. We can also provide a customer-facing data processing addendum.
[08:36] Rajiv: Let's talk timeline: We want a pilot with a small district—can we get Protected PII in a sandbox?
[08:43] Diego: Yes, we can do a pilot in Private or Dedicated; Hosted could be used if we set an isolated tenant and CMK. For sandboxing PII we recommend Private with your KMS.
[08:53] Elena: Cost—any rough numbers for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool vs Private 4-GPU in our tenant? We need a ballpark to present to finance.
[09:01] Maya: I'll send a ballpark cost sheet. Generally Dedicated includes infra + managed service premium; Private has a license fee plus infra and ops. Diego will prepare a latency/cost matrix to help tradeoff decisions.
[09:12] Samantha: Ok, technical detail ask: For audit log retention 7 years, are you ok with logs being exported to our S3 with MFA delete and Glacier Vault Lock?
[09:22] Diego: That's fine. We can stream to your S3 and you can apply MFA Delete and Vault Lock. We'll document the pipeline and ensure log signatures for tamper evidence.
[09:32] Rajiv: On the SCIM mapping, we need to map Okta groups to fine-grained roles and prevent privilege escalation from group sync. Is there RBAC change approval/workflow?
[09:42] Diego: We support approval workflows and can integrate with your ticketing system for privileged role changes; for Private we can also require sign-off via your internal processes.
[09:51] Samantha: Are there any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of — e.g., for telemetry or monitoring?
[09:57] Maya: We use a handful of cloud vendors and telemetry providers; the security pack will list subprocessors and data flow. For Private deployments subprocessor surface is much smaller.
[10:06] Elena: On encryption key rotation — do you support automatic rotation or do we manage it?
[10:10] Diego: If keys are in your KMS you control rotation. For hosted-managed CMKs we rotate per our policy but can sync rotation windows with customers.
[10:18] Samantha: Final thing — procurement will ask about indemnity and data breach financial terms. We'll need to get legal w/ a standard vendor agreement and then negotiate those clauses.
[10:28] Maya: Understood. We'll provide standard contract language and surface those items to our legal team early.
[10:33] Maya: Quick recap of next steps and action items?
[10:36] Samantha: sure
[10:37] Diego: Action items: Maya to send SOC2/ISO and security pack; Diego to prepare Dedicated vs Private perf/cost matrix and KMS options; Elena to share Aurora's data residency and FERPA constraints doc; schedule a follow-up with infra deep-dive in 1 week.
[10:52] Maya: Excellent. Any remaining questions?
[10:54] Samantha: No major ones, just want the security pack and pen-test summary.
[10:58] Rajiv: We'll review and get legal engaged.
[11:00] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and a proposed calendar for the infra call.

End of transcript (auto-trimmed).
